The Index's SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes relevant data and defines the License criterion in its admission table. Section 3.1 of the identified edition supplies the grant that the table requires.

challenge.method: Compared the versioned full-text heading, grant and §4.4 with the other two ODC v1.0 instruments. Checked whether the linked summary or plain-text edition could stand for the pinned HTML and whether the database grant reached copyright in individual contents.
challenge.results: The page distinguishes this representation from its summary and plain text. ODbL §4.4 addresses share alike, ODC-By §4.4 addresses licensing of others, and PDDL §3 begins with dedication. Under ODbL §§2.3–2.4, operating programs and independent copyright in individual contents fall outside the grant. Database Rights and contract can still bear on extraction or use.

limitations: Active is the intended Index lifecycle value. Current admission, adoption by a public-sector body, rights in a particular work, redistribution and installation require separate evidence.

reasoning: Open Data Commons identifies its English full legal text as “Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0.” Section 3.1 grants a license to use the Database, and §4.4 sets share-alike conditions for publicly used derivative databases. This satisfies the Index criterion of an identifiable grant, text and edition from a controlling source. The database grant supports the data branch of the claim. SCES §§1–4 require authority for the particular proposition, a pinned representation, and a challenge to a proposed identity merge. The publisher establishes the instrument and the Index establishes the classification criterion.
